heading: Death Metal Cat — Game Design Document
text:
Draft v4 — MAIGD1 Capstone Submission · Prepared with active development progress as of this submission.
Changelog from v3: Section 4.2's agent-roster table updated with real, git-log-verified statuses and commit hashes for Foundation Extractor (GDD-ingestion + live-vs-header constants check, commit 432637d), Reachability Verifier (built and proven, commit e64dba1), and Stress Tester (built and proven, commit 187f856) — all three now share one math core (compute_gaps(), compute_derived_movement_constants()) rather than duplicated logic. Level & Encounter Designer and Balance/QA Reviewer statuses corrected against git log rather than carried forward from v2 assumption: Level & Encounter Designer is proven end-to-end (commit 553a007), not "in progress"; Balance/QA Reviewer is committed (commit 947e7fd), not "not yet committed." New Tools/room_status.json tracking file documented (Section 4.2) as the manual, human-maintained gate for which rooms are eligible for stress-testing.
Changelog from v2 (carried forward): Sections 2.6, 3, and 4.2–4.3 rewritten to reflect the retirement of the fixed-vocabulary Room Geometry Designer in favor of the measured golden-room pipeline. Enemy System (2.7) updated to reflect the completed ranged-attack rewrite. Agent role name "Room Geometry Designer" is preserved for continuity; only its internal method changed.

heading: 1. Executive Summary
text:
Death Metal Cat is a fast-paced 2D side-scrolling action game. The player controls Cayde, a deep-voiced, growling cat fighting through a branching city gauntlet with sword and gun, building a "Gnarly" style rank through aggressive, hit-focused combat.
Core loop: platform through a room → fight enemies with sword/gun → dodge or wall-jump out of danger → land hits to build Gnarly Rank (which boosts melee damage) → clear the room → advance one-way into the next room (sometimes choosing between two branching paths) → repeat across 8 rooms → reach the end of the biome.
Win condition: reach the Biome End marker at the far side of Room 8, having advanced through all 8 rooms in a single run (Rooms 1–3, a branch through 4A or 4B, reconverging at 5, then 6–8).
Loss / fail state: death sends Cayde all the way back to Room 1 — a full restart of the run, not a soft checkpoint respawn. Health, Gnarly Rank, and all room progress reset together; reaching Room 6 and then dying means walking back through Rooms 1–5 again to return to where you fell. This is a deliberate roguelike-style stakes mechanic: it makes each run's later rooms feel genuinely tense rather than consequence-free, and gives the branching room structure (Section 2.6) more replay weight, since a full restart means seeing the other Room 3 branch on a subsequent attempt.
Scope note: This is a single-biome capstone slice. Full commercial vision is a multi-biome roguelike (city → forest → …, each ending in a boss), but this document and the current build target one complete biome — a branching, room-based city level — as the actual deliverable. Systems are built to extend to additional biomes later without rework.

heading: 2. Game Mechanics
text: This section describes what the player actually sees and does, moment to moment.

heading: 2.1 Player Verbs
text:
Verb | Input | Notes | Status
Move Left/Right | Standard 2D lateral movement | — | Done
Jump | Jump button | Platforming traversal | Done
Sword Attack | Melee button | Primary damage, builds Gnarly Rank | Done
Gun Fire | Ranged button | Secondary damage; hold-fire loop; hitscan via sphere-trace tolerance | Done
Dodge | Dodge button | i-frames; backward launch, facing-locked | Done
Wall Slide | Hold toward wall (airborne) | Reduced fall speed against a wall surface | Done
Wall Jump | Jump while wall-sliding | Launches up and away from the wall; brief input lockout | Done
Air Down Shot | Gun Fire while airborne | Fixed 45° downward shot with dedicated animation | Done
Stretch goal, not this deliverable: Double Jump (planned as a future unlockable skill), full combo canceling, aerial combo variants.

heading: 2.2 Gnarly Ranking System
text:
Landing hits (sword or gun) accumulates hit-count toward the next rank tier: 10 / 20 / 40 / 70 hits.
Taking any hit causes a full reset — all rank progress drops to zero. High-risk, high-reward: rewards sustained aggression, punishes mistakes.
Each rank tier grants a flat melee damage boost (+5% per tier, multiplies with Strength rather than adding).
On-screen rank meter plus an escalating 5-stage face-portrait HUD element (calm → glowing red eyes at max rank).
Status: Done and verified through real enemy contact, not just manual damage calls.

heading: 2.3 RPG Attribute System
text:
Simplified from original design — auto-apply on level-up rather than an interactive allocation screen, to avoid building a separate UI/input-focus paradigm this close to deadline.
Attribute | Effect
Speed | Movement speed
Strength | Sword damage — multiplies with Gnarly Rank bonus
Dexterity | Gun damage
Defense | Damage resistance, clamped at 90% max
Flat XP per kill; flat level curve (Level × 50); +2 to all attributes per level; cap at level 30.
Skill Points banked per level for a future combo/special-move system (not yet built — tracked only).
Status: Done and verified via before/after damage comparison across a level-up.

heading: 2.4 Player Health & Death/Respawn
text:
Health bar HUD with live color shift (green → yellow/orange → red) as Health depletes.
Low-health screen effect: smooth-scaling reddish dim below 25% Health, fading in/out rather than snapping.
On death: brief animation, input disabled, then after a short delay a full run restart — the room progression state resets to Room 1 (whatever room was active deactivates, Room 1 reactivates), the player is teleported to Room 1's actual start position, and Health and Gnarly Rank both reset to zero. There is no partial/checkpoint respawn; death always sends the player back to the very beginning of the biome. A brief post-restart invulnerability window prevents an immediate re-death standing in the same spot.
Design rationale: a full restart-on-death (rather than a soft checkpoint) is a deliberate choice to give the run real stakes and make the branching room structure (Section 2.6) replay-relevant — dying late still costs the whole run, and a subsequent attempt may take the other Room 3 branch.
Status: Done and verified — full-restart-to-Room1 behavior (room-progression reset and exit-trigger re-arming for a repeat pass) built and verified across both branch paths.

heading: 2.5 Dialogue & Humor (Quip Display)
text:
The first fully-proven AI agent in the pipeline (see Section 4.2). Generates short, in-character one-liners triggered by kill / damage-taken / environment-interaction events, displayed in a JRPG-style dialogue box (portrait + name label + text, bottom-left of screen, auto-fade after a few seconds).
Voice: deep, rough, growl-heavy one-liners — not clever banter. No cutesy cat-speak; "meow" only as a short, aggressive, bark-like sound when used at all.
Two-layer pacing: each trigger type (kill/damage/environment) has its own long cooldown (5 min) so the same type doesn't repeat too often, plus a short global debounce (~6s) so two different trigger types can't fire back-to-back and overwhelm the player.
Pipeline: batch-generated via the Claude API → hand-curated (41 quips currently locked in) → imported into a UE5 DataTable → read at runtime with zero live API dependency during gameplay.
Status: Done, committed, and re-verified end-to-end after a commit-split reconstruction.

heading: 2.6 Level Structure & Progression
text:
The city biome is a branching, one-way room sequence: 9 authored room shells, of which any single playthrough passes through 8 (Rooms 1–3, a branch to 4A or 4B, both reconverging at Room 5, then 6–8). Room 8 currently ends in a placeholder "end of biome" marker — a full boss encounter is a stretch goal, not in this deliverable.
Progression is strictly one-way: once a room is exited, its geometry and collision deactivate — there is no backtracking.
[UPDATED v3] Room platforming geometry, including 2D sprite dressing, is agent-generated via a measured golden-room pipeline rather than a fixed piece vocabulary: a Foundation Extractor agent measures a hand-built "golden" reference room per biome — platform spacing, jump/wall-jump/dodge reachability, and 2D sprite scale/color-value consistency — all queried live against Cayde's actual current movement constants, never hardcoded. This produces a per-biome spec file that a Room Variation Generator consumes to compose new room layouts, reusing the same measured spacing and matching visual dressing rather than geometry alone.
[UPDATED v3] Two independent checks run before anything ships: a Reachability Verifier re-checks every generated gap against the golden room's measured constants (the same deterministic, non-LLM check philosophy as before — physical reachability is verified in code, not trusted to model judgment), and a Stress Tester checks deeper edge cases — e.g. whether a room's validity survives a later movement-constant retune, or whether a "reachable" gap is only reachable via a frame-perfect input rather than a comfortable one.
A Python import script then places the validated, dressed layout directly into UE5 as real actors, including enemy/pickup spawn markers positioned within the generated geometry — the human role is reviewing and hand-tweaking the generated result (repositioning a platform, widening a gap, adjusting dressing) rather than building rooms, or their art, from scratch.

heading: Status:
text:
Room progression framework (branching, one-way gating): built, tested via both branches, and committed.
[UPDATED v4] Room Geometry Designer (measured-golden-room method): proven on Room1 — Foundation Extractor built, committed, and verified (biome_spec_AssassinCity.json, hash-verified output, commit 432637d), including GDD-ingestion and a live-vs-C++-header movement-constants check that halts before measuring on a genuine mismatch (this caught and led to fixing a real 9.1% JumpZVelocity drift). Room Variation Generator: 6 test room variations were generated reusing Room1's platforms, walkways, and 2D dressing with minimal manual correction, then removed as scratch; Room2 and Room3 were subsequently built manually via the same golden-room asset-reuse approach. Full asset-pool-driven generation (drawing from more than Room1's original set) is pending the Asset Cataloger, still scoped and not yet built.
[UPDATED v4] Reachability Verifier: proven, built and validated three ways — cross-checked against Foundation Extractor's own output, a synthetic too-wide-gap test, and real runs against Room1 and Room2 (commit e64dba1). Stress Tester: proven, built and validated against Room1 (stored-baseline diff), Room2 (fresh live recompute — this uncovered and fixed a real bug where the initial draft silently reused Room1's stored gaps for Room2), and Room3 (clean status-gate skip via the new Tools/room_status.json, manually maintained per-room per-biome) (commit 187f856). Both share one math core with Foundation Extractor (compute_gaps(), compute_derived_movement_constants()) rather than duplicating reachability logic.
Known open issue (carried from v2, status unconfirmed — verify before next milestone): room-to-room exit triggers, originally positioned against the old flat placeholder floors, previously appeared misaligned against real imported geometry. Root cause was under active investigation as of the prior draft; confirm current status before relying on this note.
Logged here rather than left silent, per the project's own practice of documenting known gaps rather than presenting untested work as finished.

heading: 2.7 Enemy System
text:
Base enemy class with detection radius, direct-approach movement (no full pathfinding at this scale), melee-range contact damage on a cooldown, hit-flash feedback, and auto-respawn.
[UPDATED v3] Ranged-attack enemy type built and committed: a three-band Tick() behavior (melee / shoot / chase) with facing-flip and a Drawing→Firing burst state machine, mirroring the player character's own hold-fire pattern, plus a dedicated AEnemyProjectile actor for spawned shots. DeathBotWalking and DeathBotFlying Blueprint content, and their Meshy-sourced art, are in place — the "additional enemy art already exists and will be swapped in during a later pass" note from v2 is resolved; the swap has happened.
Status: Done and verified — confirmed to correctly trigger the player's Hurt animation, i-frames, and Gnarly Rank reset through real contact, not just console-command damage. Ranged-attack system compiled clean and verified via DLL-timestamp check.

heading: 3. AI Architecture
text:
This section describes each agent purely through its effect on what the player experiences — the technical input/output details, schemas, and build status for each live in Section 4 (Technical Strategy).
Agent | Development role (one sentence) | Effect the player actually sees/feels
Quip Generator | Writes Cayde's short, growled one-liner reactions offline, ahead of time, so nothing is generated live during play. | A JRPG-style dialogue box (Cayde's portrait + a line of text) pops in whenever the player lands a kill, takes damage, or triggers certain environment interactions — never more than once every few seconds, and never the same line twice in a row.
Room Geometry Designer (team) | [UPDATED v3] Builds each room's actual jump-gap-and-platform layout, and its 2D dressing, from a golden room measured once per biome — not a fixed piece vocabulary — checked against Cayde's real, live-queried jump/wall-jump/dodge reach so nothing impossible ever gets placed. | Later rooms in a run feel physically harder to traverse than earlier ones — bigger gaps, more wall-jump sections — because the difficulty curve is baked into the level geometry itself, not just enemy count. Generated rooms also carry consistent visual dressing, not bare greybox.
Level & Encounter Designer | Decides how many enemies and pickups actually appear at the spawn points the Room Geometry Designer left inside each room. | Early rooms feel sparse and forgiving; later rooms feel busier and more dangerous, with pickups spaced to matter most early and become scarcer as tension rises near the end of the run.
Balance/QA Reviewer | Reads a generated room's enemy/pickup layout before it ships and flags anything that looks mathematically unfair (e.g. a room requiring more health than a player could plausibly have at that point). | The player never sees this agent directly — its job is making sure the difficulty curve they feel across the run is intentional, not an accidental spike from a generation mistake.

heading: 4.1 Engine & Bridge
text:
Engine: Unreal Engine 5, Paper2D enabled for sprite sheet integration.
Agent bridge: UE5's Python Editor Scripting API (unreal module) via Remote Execution, allowing Claude Code to drive the editor externally.
Status: verified and in active daily use — asset import, actor placement, live property queries, and diagnostic scripts all run routinely through this bridge, not just as an initial proof-of-concept.

heading: 4.2 Agent Roster — Technical Detail (Pillar 1 — AI Dev Pipeline)
text:
Agent | Role | Input | Output | Status
Quip Generator | Writes a short in-character line + sound-bite tag for kill/damage/environment triggers. | Trigger type, character profile | JSON: line + sound tag | Proven end-to-end
Foundation Extractor | Measures a hand-built golden room once per biome: platform/gap spacing and reachability (jump/wall-jump/dodge, live-queried against the character CDO, never hardcoded), plus 2D sprite scale and HSV color-value consistency across placed instances. [UPDATED v4] Also ingests the GDD (Death_Metal_Cat_GDD_v3.docx) once, extracts room roles and the agent roster, and halts before measuring anything if the GDD's documented movement-constant categories don't reconcile with a live-vs-C++-header-default comparison beyond a 1% relative tolerance — this caught and led to fixing a real 9.1% JumpZVelocity drift between the live-tuned Blueprint and the stale C++ header default. | Golden room level asset, GDD (read once, passed downstream as structured data) | biome_spec_<Biome>.json, gdd_reference.json | [UPDATED v4] Proven — measurement/spec pipeline hash-verified on Room1/AssassinCity; GDD-ingestion + constants-halt built and verified this pass (commit 432637d)
Room Variation Generator | Composes a new room's platforming layout and 2D dressing by drawing on biome_spec.json's measured spacing/reachability rules, rather than a fixed piece vocabulary. Places enemy/pickup spawn markers within the generated geometry. | biome_spec.json, gdd_reference.json, cataloged asset pool (Asset Cataloger, in progress) | JSON: ordered piece sequence + spawn marker positions + dressing assignments | In progress — 6 test room variations generated and since removed as scratch; Room2 and Room3 built manually via the same golden-room asset-reuse method and independently confirmed reachable by Reachability Verifier. Full asset-pool-driven generation pending Asset Cataloger.
Reachability Verifier | Independently re-checks every gap in a room against biome_spec.json's measured movement constants — the deterministic (non-LLM) validation pass. compute_gaps() is extracted as a single shared function so Foundation Extractor and Reachability Verifier can never drift out of sync with each other. | Room's live platform actors, biome_spec.json | Pass/fail per gap + flagged issues | [UPDATED v4] Proven — built, and validated three ways (cross-check against Foundation Extractor's own output on Room1, a synthetic too-wide-gap test, and real runs against Room1/Room2) (commit e64dba1)
Stress Tester | Answers two questions Reachability Verifier's binary pass/fail doesn't: whether a room's PASS is still trustworthy if movement constants have drifted since biome_spec.json was generated, and whether a technically-reachable gap is comfortable or needs manual playtest confirmation (tight-margin flag, ≥85% of max range — the OneWayPlatform11→15 lesson: formula-reachable isn't automatically playtest-trustworthy). Gated by Tools/room_status.json (nested per biome, three states: not_started / in_progress / finished) so an unfinished room is cleanly skipped rather than falsely flagged as failing. | Room's live state, biome_spec.json, gdd_reference.json, room_status.json | stress_test_<Room>.json: drift findings + comfortable_pass / tight_pass_needs_playtest / fail per gap | [UPDATED v4] Proven — built, reuses compute_gaps() and a newly-extracted compute_derived_movement_constants() as shared math with Foundation Extractor; validated against Room1 (source-room baseline), Room2 (fresh recompute), and Room3 (clean status-gate skip) (commit 187f856)
Asset Cataloger | Scans a folder of biome assets (beyond the fixed set already measured in Room1) and outputs footprint, alignment, layer, and role data per asset, so the Room Variation Generator can draw freely from a growing asset pool rather than a hand-fixed set. | Asset folder, biome name | asset_catalog_<Biome>.json | Scoped, not yet built
Level & Encounter Designer | Given a room's difficulty tier and the spawn markers left in the generated geometry, decides what (if anything) populates each marker — enemy type or pickup type — driving an escalating difficulty curve across the run. | Difficulty tier + room's marker list | JSON: per-marker population decision | [CORRECTED v4 — v2/v3 text was stale, verified against git log] Proven — built, committed, and verified against all 9 real rooms (commit 553a007, 2026-07-23)
Balance/QA Reviewer | Reads level/encounter output and flags risk spikes or scaling issues. | Encounter JSON, attribute progression curve | Flagged issues + rationale | [CORRECTED v4 — v2/v3 text was stale, verified against git log] Committed (commit 947e7fd, 2026-08-03) — draft implementation exists and is committed; verification against real Level & Encounter Designer output not yet re-confirmed
No orchestration agent — at this scale (single biome, expanded room-geometry sub-team plus two remaining agents), manual routing between pipeline stages is simpler and cheaper than a dedicated orchestration agent.

heading: 4.3 Technical Requirements & Constraints (Pillar 2)
text:
Human gates — tasks agents explicitly do not do:
Sprite/portrait art creation (manual image-generation passes, curated by hand — including new wall-slide and air-down-shot frames added mid-build).
Sound implementation — text quips plus placeholder sound-bite tags; no voice acting; placing real audio assets is manual.
Physics/collision setup fundamentals (initial capsule/collision profile tuning) — hand-authored; downstream room geometry is agent-generated but built on these human-set foundations.
Final room review and hand-tweaking — the Room Variation Generator produces validated, physically-reachable, dressed layouts, but a human reviews each generated room in-editor and adjusts anything that reads poorly (visual variety, exact platform feel) rather than accepting agent output uncritically.
Final combat feel and tuning — agents can flag a numeric spike; whether it's actually fun is a human judgment call.
[UPDATED v3] Process rule: every biome's spec (biome_spec_<Biome>.json) is measured against a specific live snapshot of Cayde's movement constants (jump distance, air control, wall-jump reach/commitment, dodge distance) at Foundation Extractor run time. If those values are ever retuned during later polish, previously generated rooms are not automatically re-validated — the Foundation Extractor must be re-run against the golden room (or the Stress Tester must confirm the drift doesn't break existing rooms) before that content can be trusted again. This has already happened once during development (JumpZVelocity, AirControl, and WallJumpCommitmentDuration were all found to have drifted from their documented C++ defaults) and is treated as an expected, recurring event, not an edge case.
Engine-side constraint: agents run offline, pre-build — they generate JSON consumed by Python import scripts during Editor time, never live calls during gameplay.

heading: 4.4 Token Budgets & API Constraints (Pillar 3)
text:
Named constraint: Claude Pro subscriptions (used for Claude Code development work) do not include programmatic API access — confirmed directly by attempting to generate an API key against the course-provided Pro account, which exposes no Console/billing access at all. Any agent that needs to run as a script calling the Claude API requires a separate, individually-billed API account rather than riding on a Pro subscription. This was discovered mid-build and required setting up API billing separately before the Quip Generator could run — a real, already-encountered constraint, not a hypothetical one.
Development-work track: Claude Code sessions run against Claude Pro subscription usage (two accounts available — personal and course-provided — switched via separate config directories when one hits its limit).
Agent-execution track: standalone agent scripts run against separate, pay-per-token API billing on a personal account.
Observed cost so far: the Quip Generator's full curation batch (45 short quips across 3 trigger types, Claude Sonnet, roughly 40 words / ~60-80 tokens of output per quip plus a short system+user prompt per call) completed for a cost on the order of cents, not dollars — each call is small and independent, well under per-request token limits.
Projected budget for the remaining agents: Foundation Extractor, Room Variation Generator, Reachability Verifier, and Level & Encounter Designer calls are similarly small (short JSON in, short JSON out) — generating and regenerating room layouts several times over during iteration is projected to stay in the same low-single-dollar range as the Quip Generator batch did, since generation happens offline in small bursts rather than continuously or per-playthrough.

heading: 5. Explicit Out-of-Scope (v1 — this deliverable)
text:
Full boss encounters (Room 8 currently ends in a placeholder marker; stretch goal).
Multiple full biomes (city only for this deliverable; architecture supports adding more later).
Full voice acting.
Skill trees / unlockable abilities beyond the already-banked Skill Points (Double Jump planned as a future unlock, not built).
Combo canceling / juggle mechanics.
Interactive level-up attribute allocation screen (auto-applied instead, see Section 5).
Full hand-animated, high-fidelity art pass (greybox/placeholder acceptable for capstone; real city tileset art is in research/sourcing now — 2D dressing for generated rooms is further along than this note previously suggested, see Section 2.6).
